correctness.rationale: Grouping by gcd gives H(n)=h(n)/n, with h(p^e)=(p^{2e+1}+1)/(p+1). For p=3 or p≡1 mod 3 the factor is a unit; for p≡2 mod 3 odd-power LTE gives v3(2e+1). Thus n=3^a m contributes exactly when a>K(m), including n=1 and equality a=K(m). Summing the geometric tail gives the frozen Dirichlet series. The coefficients of p^{-s} at p≡2 are canceled by exponents α(s)=(1+3^{-s})/2 and β(s)=(1−3^{-s})/2; the residual product is holomorphic and bounded uniformly for Re s≥3/4 by the O(p^{-2 Re s}) local bound. For the variable-exponent extraction, take x half-integral, c=1+1/log x and T=exp(sqrt(log x)). The bounded coefficients give truncated Perron error O(x log x/T). In a narrower classical zero-free strip Re s≥1−c0/log T, away from a disk about 1, the holomorphic logs of ζ and L are O(log log(|t|+3)) for large |t| (Borel–Carathéodory with the center to the right of 1 and the near-1-line polylog bounds on ζ and L); thus bounded α,β give polylog growth. The horizontal sides and the left side are negligible, the latter by x^{-c0/log T}, also absorbing the O((log T)^{2/3}) bound near the cut. The jump of (s−1)^{-2/3} gives 1/Γ(2/3); the logarithmic error contributes O(x log log x/(log x)^{4/3}) by integrating e^{-u log x}u^{1/3}log(1/u) along the cut. This avoids assuming an analytic factor after extracting the fixed exponent. L(1,χ)=∫_0^1 dt/(1+t+t²)=π/(3√3), and the 3-factor is (2/3)^{2/3}/2. Every real local factor is positive and first-order cancellation makes the product converge absolutely. No discrepancy found. The independent finite check compared exact rational gcd sums to the criterion through 500 and recounted 1479, 13507, 64093 at 10^4, 10^5, 5·10^5 by prime-power valuation accumulation. This corroborates the arithmetic, not the asymptotic.
residual_risks: Finite counts and the recorded prime cutoff do not certify the asymptotic or a decimal error bound on C3. The argument fixes the prime 3.

value.rationale: The smallest odd prime gives a natural local obstruction for an established integrality problem. A zero-density result alone permits widely different counting functions; identifying the 1/3 decay and actual constant quantifies the competition between the exponent at 3 and cancellation from other prime powers. This is more than another finite table of denominator values or an arbitrary slice of an invariant.
residual_risks: No statement about other primes, complete integrality, or a certified numerical value of the constant.
